claim: Cytotoxic immune cells are endowed with a high degree of heterogeneity in their lytic function.
source: Cytotoxic immune cells are endowed with a high degree of heterogeneity in their lytic function, but how this heterogeneity is generated is still an open question.
evidence: This is stated as background context in the abstract, framing the research question.

claim: CD107a+-intracellular vesicles, perforin, and granzyme B unevenly segregate in a constant fraction of telophasic cells during each division round.
source: We show that CD107a+-intracellular vesicles, perforin, and granzyme B unevenly segregate in a constant fraction of telophasic cells during each division round.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by imaging flow cytometry data in Figure 1.

claim: Unequal lytic molecule inheritance by daughter cells results from the random distribution of lytic granules on the two sides of the cleavage furrow.
source: Mathematical modeling posits that unequal lytic molecule inheritance by daughter cells results from the random distribution of lytic granules on the two sides of the cleavage furrow.
evidence: This claim is supported by mathematical modeling presented in the manuscript.

claim: The level of lytic compartment in individual cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) dictates CTL killing capacity.
source: Finally, we establish that the level of lytic compartment in individual cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) dictates CTL killing capacity.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 7.

claim: Individual mouse and human lymphocytes exhibit high degrees of heterogeneity in both their phenotypic and functional characteristics.
source: Accordingly, several studies put forth the notion that individual mouse and human lymphocytes exhibit high degrees of heterogeneity in both their phenotypic and functional characteristics (Beuneu et al., 2010; Buchholz et al., 2016; Buchholz et al., 2013; Ganesan et al., 2017; Kumar et al., 2018; Lemaître et al., 2013; Newell et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Human CTL belonging to the same clonal population exhibit heterogeneity in their lytic function during sustained interaction with target cells.
source: Accordingly, we have previously shown that human CTL belonging to the same clonal population exhibit heterogeneity in their lytic function during sustained interaction with target cells (Vasconcelos et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Some CTL kill a limited number of target cells, while others emerge as super-killer cells.
source: While some CTL kill a limited number of target cells, others emerge as super-killer cells.
evidence: This is stated as a known observation from previous research.

claim: Asymmetric cell division (ACD) plays a crucial role in embryogenesis by allowing the formation of two distinct cells from a single mother cell.
source: It plays a crucial role in embryogenesis by allowing the formation of two distinct cells from a single mother cell (Dewey et al., 2015; Knoblich, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: ACD has been proposed as a process allowing mouse naive T lymphocytes to divide into short-lived effector T cells and memory T cells, after TCR-triggered division.
source: In immunology, ACD has been proposed as a process allowing mouse naive T lymphocytes to divide into short-lived effector T cells and memory T cells, after TCR-triggered division (Arsenio et al., 2015; Arsenio et al., 2014; Chang et al., 2011; Chang et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: 23% of telophasic CD8+ T cells exhibited an uneven distribution of CD107a+ vesicles overcoming the 40–60% CTV range.
source: As shown in Figure 1A, while CTV distribution ranged between 40 and 60% in dividing T cells, 23% of telophasic CD8+ T cells exhibited an uneven distribution of CD107a+ vesicles overcoming the 40–60% CTV range.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from imaging flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Perforin and granzyme B unevenly segregated into the two nascent daughter cells in telophase.
source: As shown in Figure 1B,C, perforin and GrzB also unevenly segregated into the two nascent daughter cells in telophase, indicating that daughter cells received a heterogeneous quantity of lytic components.
evidence: This is supported by imaging flow cytometry data shown in Figures 1B and 1C.

claim: The slope of the linear regression curve for the distribution of CD107a, perforin, and GrzB as compared to CTV was close to 0.1.
source: The slope of the linear regression curve for the distribution of CD107a, perforin, and GrzB as compared to CTV was close to 0.1, indicating that these three molecules distributed independently from total proteins.
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of the data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Memory CD8+ T cells exhibited uneven repartition of CD107a and perforin in telophase.
source: This analysis showed that also memory CD8+ T cells exhibited uneven repartition of CD107a and perforin in telophase (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: 15% of the two nascent daughter cells in telophase of clonal CTL exhibited uneven distribution of CD107a.
source: As shown in Figure 1D, we observed that in clonal CTL undergoing cell division, 15% of the two nascent daughter cells in telophase exhibited uneven distribution of CD107a, thus confirming and extending observations obtained using CD8+ peripheral blood T cells.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from imaging flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: A lysosomal-associated membrane protein and effector molecules involved in CTL lytic function unevenly segregate in 10–23% of individual human CD8+ T cells undergoing division.
source: Taken together, the above results indicate that a lysosomal-associated membrane protein known to be a marker of lytic granules and effector molecules involved in CTL lytic function, unevenly segregate in 10–23% of individual human CD8+ T cells undergoing division.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the imaging flow cytometry data presented in Figure 1.

claim: 27% of the CD8+ T cells in telophase exhibited uneven repartition of CD107a, above a 1.5 threshold, as measured by confocal laser scanning microscopy.
source: Although this approach allowed us to collect a relatively small number of cells in telophase (n = 61 compared to n = 908 obtained by image flow cytometry), it revealed that 27% of the CD8+ T cells in telophase exhibited uneven repartition of CD107a, above a 1.5 threshold (corresponding to the 40–60% range used in imaging flow cytometry experiments) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Both T-bet and c-Myc did not unevenly segregate into the two nascent daughter cells during telophase.
source: As shown in Figure 3A,B, both T-bet and c-Myc did not unevenly segregate into the two nascent daughter cells during telophase.
evidence: This is supported by imaging flow cytometry data shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: The slope of the linear regression curve for the distribution of T-bet and c-Myc as compared to CTV was close to 1.
source: Moreover, the slope of the linear regression curve for the distribution of T-bet and c-Myc as compared to CTV was close to 1, indicating that the repartition of these two molecules in telophase followed that of total proteins.
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of the data presented in Figure 3.

claim: A polarity cue was not required to induce uneven distribution of lytic molecules.
source: Figure 4A,B shows that a polarity cue was not required to induce uneven distribution of lytic molecules, since comparable CD107a+ vesicle segregation was observed in peripheral blood CD8+ T cells stimulated by either immobilized (anti-CD3/anti-CD28/ICAM-1) or soluble (phorbol myristate acetate+ ionomycin) stimuli.
evidence: This is supported by comparative data shown in Figures 4A and 4B.

claim: Uneven partitioning of lytic compartment in telophase is not associated with asymmetric segregation of fate determining transcription factors.
source: Overall, the above results demonstrate that uneven partitioning of lytic compartment in telophase is not associated with asymmetric segregation of fate determining transcription factors.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data showing no asymmetric distribution of T-bet and c-Myc.

claim: In human CD8+ T cells, lytic machinery uneven repartition is not related to described mechanisms of fate determining ACD.
source: All in all, the above results show that, in human CD8+ T cells, lytic machinery uneven repartition is not related to described mechanisms of fate determining ACD.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data showing no asymmetric distribution of fate-determining factors and no requirement for polarity cues.

claim: In all division rounds considered, a comparable percentage of cells underwent heterogeneous repartition of CD107a.
source: This analysis showed that, in all division rounds considered, a comparable percentage of cells underwent heterogeneous repartition of CD107a (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 5A and 5B.

claim: Cells undergoing uneven repartition of lytic machinery in telophase were randomly distributed all over the CD107a expression curves.
source: The χ2 statistical test showed that cells undergoing uneven repartition of lytic machinery in telophase were randomly distributed all over the CD107a expression curves (See Materials and methods).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on statistical analysis of the data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The heterogeneity process is stationary, but not hereditary: a daughter cell originating from a heterogeneous division has a constant stationary probability to produce a new uneven division.
source: A complementary observation indicated that the heterogeneity process is stationary, but not hereditary: for example a daughter cell originating from a heterogeneous division has a constant stationary probability to produce a new uneven division.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on statistical analysis of the data.

claim: The Kolmogorov–Smirnov goodness-of-fit test rejected the hypothesis that the CD107a expression curves follow the same distribution at the different division rounds.
source: The Kolmogorov–Smirnov goodness-of-fit test rejected the hypothesis that the CD107a expression curves follow the same distribution at the different division round (see Supplementary Results).
evidence: This is a result from statistical analysis of the data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The χ2 test showed that variability was distributed all over the curves.
source: The χ2 test showed that variability was distributed all over the curves.
evidence: This is a result from statistical analysis of the data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Kolmogorov–Smirnov goodness-of-fit and χ2 tests revealed a non-stationary variability in the content of CD107a+ vesicles in CD8+ T cells during early division events.
source: Together, Kolmogorov–Smirnov goodness-of-fit and χ2 tests revealed a non-stationary variability in the content of CD107a+ vesicles in CD8+ T cells during early division events.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on statistical analysis of the data.

claim: Asymmetric distribution of CD107a+ vesicles in telophase is not limited to the first division, but it is rather a stochastic process, inherent to each division, that perpetuates variability in daughter cells.
source: Taken together, the above results indicate that asymmetric distribution of CD107a+ vesicles in telophase is not limited to the first division, but it is rather a stochastic process, inherent to each division, that perpetuates variability in daughter cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data showing comparable percentages of asymmetric divisions across division rounds.

claim: mCherry-tagged GrzB showed no preferential localization within cell cytosol at the different phases of the division and appeared to randomly partition into the two nascent daughter cells.
source: mCherry-tagged GrzB showed no preferential localization within cell cytosol at the different phases of the division and appeared to randomly partition into the two nascent daughter cells.
evidence: This is an observation from live-cell microscopy experiments shown in Figure 6A and 6B.

claim: For n < 100 lytic granules, the probabilities that individual particles distribute asymmetrically on the two sides of the cleavage furrow are relatively high.
source: This analysis showed that for n < 100 the probabilities that individual particles distribute asymmetrically on the two sides of the cleavage furrow are relatively high (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a result from mathematical modeling shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Using stimulated emission depletion (STED) on CTL stained for GrzB, 14–65 (mean = 37) lytic granules are contained within individual CTL.
source: Using stimulated emission depletion (STED) on CTL stained for GrzB, we estimated that 14–65 (mean = 37) lytic granules are contained within individual CTL.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from STED microscopy.

claim: The estimation of 14–65 lytic granules per CTL well matched with numbers published in previous studies, ranging between 10 and 100.
source: Our estimation well matched with numbers published in previous studies, ranging between 10 and 100 (Chiang et al., 2017; Clark et al., 2003; Kataoka et al., 1996; Peters et al., 1991).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: For a probability of 20% asymmetric repartition of particles, particle correlation has a relatively low value (4% for 37 particles, 0.04; CI 95%, 0.035–0.045).
source: The analysis shows that for a probability of 20% asymmetric repartition of particles (corresponding to 20% uneven repartition of lytic granules during cell division experimentally measured by imaging flow cytometry and confocal imaging), particle correlation has a relatively low value (4% for 37 particles, 0.04; CI 95%, 0.035–0.045), suggesting that lytic granules mainly segregate independently during cell division.
evidence: This is a result from Monte-Carlo simulation analysis.

claim: The observed stationary unequal distribution of lytic granules in telophase is the result of a stochastic repartition of particulate cytosolic structures on the two sides of the cleavage furrow in dividing cells.
source: Taken together, cell imaging and computational results strongly suggest that the observed stationary unequal distribution of lytic granules in telophase is the result of a stochastic repartition of particulate cytosolic structures on the two sides of the cleavage furrow in dividing cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on both imaging data and mathematical modeling.

claim: Sorted LysoTrackerHigh and LysoTrackerLow CTL populations maintained their difference in LysoTracker staining at least 24 hr after cell sorting.
source: As shown in Figure 7A, sorted LysoTrackerHigh and LysoTrackerLow CTL populations maintained their difference in LysoTracker staining at least 24 hr after cell sorting.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: For each ratio, LysoTrackerHigh CTL were more efficient than LysoTrackerLow CTL in exerting cytotoxicity.
source: For each ratio, LysoTrackerHigh CTL were more efficient than LysoTrackerLow CTL in exerting cytotoxicity (Figure 7B,C), although basal killing (in the absence of peptide stimulation) was comparable between LysoTrackerHigh and LysoTrackerLow CTL (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by cytotoxicity assay data shown in Figures 7B and 7C.

claim: LysoTrackerhigh CTL exhibited a higher lytic granule secretion as detected by CD107a exposure when compared to LysoTrackerlow CTL.
source: Results show that LysoTrackerhigh CTL exhibited a higher lytic granule secretion as detected by CD107a exposure when compared to LysoTrackerlow CTL (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Productive TCR engagement was comparable in both LysoTrackerhigh and LysoTrackerlow populations as detected by similar levels of CD8 internalization.
source: However, productive TCR engagement was comparable in both populations as detected by similar levels of CD8 internalization (Huang et al., 2019; Xiao et al., 2007; Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: The lytic granule cargo of individual CTL and not their activation properties directly impact killing behavior.
source: Together, these results indicate that the lytic granule cargo of individual CTL and not their activation properties directly impact killing behavior.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data showing differential killing capacity but similar TCR engagement.

claim: Stochastic uneven distribution of lytic granules in dividing CTL determine heterogeneous killing behavior at the single-cell level.
source: They imply that stochastic uneven distribution of lytic granules in dividing CTL determine heterogeneous killing behavior at the single-cell level.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined findings of asymmetric lytic granule distribution and differential killing capacity.

claim: In both freshly isolated peripheral blood CD8+ T cells and clonal CTL, ~20% of telophasic cells undergo asymmetric distribution of the lytic compartment into the two daughter cells.
source: In the present study, we found that, in both freshly isolated peripheral blood CD8+ T cells and clonal CTL, ~20% of telophasic cells undergo asymmetric distribution of the lytic compartment into the two daughter cells.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings from the study.

claim: CD8+ killing capacity is associated with lytic compartment level.
source: Our results establish that CD8+ killing capacity is associated with lytic compartment level and strongly suggest that uneven lytic machinery repartition produces CD8+ T cell populations with heterogeneous killing capacities.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data from Figure 7.

claim: Uneven lytic machinery repartition produces CD8+ T cell populations with heterogeneous killing capacities.
source: Our results establish that CD8+ killing capacity is associated with lytic compartment level and strongly suggest that uneven lytic machinery repartition produces CD8+ T cell populations with heterogeneous killing capacities.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined findings of the study.

claim: Imaging flow cytometry combines the advantages of flow cytometry and microscopy and allows the detection and analysis of rare cells within whole-cell populations on the basis of their morphological and staining characteristics.
source: We used imaging flow cytometry, a technique that combines the advantages of flow cytometry and microscopy and allows the detection and analysis of rare cells within whole-cell populations on the basis of their morphological and staining characteristics (Basiji and O'Gorman, 2015; Doan et al., 2018; Hritzo et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a description of the imaging flow cytometry technique, supported by citations.

claim: The uneven lytic machinery distribution is not related to ACD.
source: Our results demonstrate that the uneven lytic machinery distribution is not related to ACD.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data showing no asymmetric distribution of fate-determining factors.

claim: In mouse T lymphocytes, ACD has been reported as a mechanism contributing to the generation of effector/memory daughter cells following the division of an individual naive T cell in response to polarizing cues.
source: In mouse T lymphocytes, ACD has been reported as a mechanism contributing to the generation of effector/memory daughter cells following the division of an individual naive T cell in response to polarizing cues (Arsenio et al., 2015; Chang et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Establishment of asymmetry has been associated with the uneven inheritance by daughter cells of transcription factors such as c-Myc and T-bet known for their role in the induction of metabolic reprogramming and in the acquisition of T cell effector function, respectively.
source: Establishment of asymmetry has been associated with the uneven inheritance by daughter cells of transcription factors such as c-Myc and T-bet known for their role in the induction of metabolic reprogramming and in the acquisition of T cell effector function, respectively (Chang et al., 2011; Verbist et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Lytic granule repartition is not accompanied by a detectable asymmetric segregation of T-bet and c-Myc and does not require a polarity cue.
source: Our results, by showing that lytic granule repartition is not accompanied by a detectable asymmetric segregation of T-bet and c-Myc and does not require a polarity cue, suggest that the lytic machinery uneven distribution observed in human CD8+ T cells is not related to previously described ACD.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data from Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Mathematical analysis of imaging flow cytometry data provides an interpretation that is compatible with a stochastic distribution of lytic components during cell division.
source: First, mathematical analysis of our imaging flow cytometry data provides an interpretation of our results that is compatible with a stochastic distribution of lytic components during cell division.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on statistical analysis of the data.

claim: The process of asymmetric distribution is stationary in terms of the fraction of involved cells: it occurs always on a similar percentage of cells, at each division round, in different experiments and following different stimuli.
source: On the one hand, mathematical analysis shows that the process of asymmetric distribution is stationary in terms of the fraction of involved cells: for example occurs always on a similar percentage of cells, at each division round, in different experiments and following different stimuli.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on statistical analysis of the data.

claim: Lytic compartments appeared randomly distributed in cell cytosol during mitosis.
source: Instead, lytic compartments appeared randomly distributed in cell cytosol.
evidence: This is an observation from live-cell imaging experiments.

claim: Pre-packaged molecular components within a few relatively big vesicles might have higher probability to be asymmetrically partitioned in telophase than molecular components dispersed throughout the cytosol.
source: In other words, pre-packaged molecular components within a few relatively big vesicles might have higher probability to be asymmetrically partitioned in telophase than molecular components dispersed throughout the cytosol.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on mathematical modeling and observations.

claim: In a limited number of division events, granules might not segregate completely independently from each other, implying that some active mechanism of granule segregation might contribute, to a minor extent, to lytic granule repartition in telophase.
source: Moreover, it should be noted that our videos and results in Figure 6 suggest that, in a limited number of division events, granules might not segregate completely independently from each other, implying that some active mechanism of granule segregation might contribute, to a minor extent, to lytic granule repartition in telophase.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on observations from live-cell imaging.

claim: The mechanism of heterogeneity generation is for the most part stochastic and might be a general mechanism for generating heterogeneity in dividing cells.
source: Together, our results point out a mechanism of heterogeneity generation that is for the most part stochastic and might be a general mechanism for generating heterogeneity in dividing cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined findings of the study.

claim: The possibility that particulate material is unevenly distributed in telophase into two nascent daughter cells has been proposed for other organelles and in other cellular systems.
source: The possibility that particulate material is unevenly distributed in telophase into two nascent daughter cells has been proposed for other organelles and in other cellular systems (Bergeland et al., 2001; Carlton et al., 2020; Sanghavi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: In MDCK cells, microscopy analysis and mathematical modeling based on the laws of probability suggested that endosome/lysosome partitioning between daughter cells is stochastic.
source: Indeed, in MDCK cells, microscopy analysis and mathematical modeling based on the laws of probability suggested that endosome/lysosome partitioning between daughter cells is stochastic (Bergeland et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: In Dictyostelium cells, it has been demonstrated that dynein and kinesin motors drive phagosomes segregation independently of each other and stochastically.
source: Similarly, in Dictyostelium cells, it has been demonstrated that dynein and kinesin motors drive phagosomes segregation independently of each other and stochastically (Sanghavi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: This study is the first to relate a mechanism of a random segregation of organelles to functional heterogeneity of immune cells.
source: To our knowledge, our present study is the first to relate a mechanism of a random segregation of organelles to functional heterogeneity of immune cells.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the study.

claim: A mechanism of asymmetric distribution in telophase (that is stationary at each division, but not inherited by daughter cells) can be instrumental to randomly generate short-lived CTL cohorts harboring functional heterogeneity while ensuring globally reproducible antigen-specific CD8+ T cell responses.
source: We propose that a mechanism of asymmetric distribution in telophase (that is stationary at each division, but not inherited by daughter cells) can be instrumental to randomly generate short-lived CTL cohorts harboring functional heterogeneity while ensuring globally reproducible antigen-specific CD8+ T cell responses.
evidence: This is a proposed functional interpretation of the findings.

claim: This process might confer robustness to CTL responses through population averaging.
source: This process might confer robustness to CTL responses through population averaging (Buchholz et al., 2016; Hodgkin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by citations.

claim: Asymmetric segregation of internalized exogenous antigen was found to occur during B cell division.
source: It is interesting to note that our results present analogies with previously published data in which asymmetric segregation of internalized exogenous antigen was found to occur during B cell division (Thaunat et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Stochastic distribution in telophase appears to be a major mechanism ensuring a high variability of both humoral and cellular adaptive immune responses during lymphocyte clonal expansion.
source: Thus, stochastic distribution in telophase appears to be a major mechanism ensuring a high variability of both humoral and cellular adaptive immune responses during lymphocyte clonal expansion.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the findings of this study and prior research on B cells.

claim: Anti-CD3/anti-CD28/ICAM-1 stimulation resulted in activation of human CD8+ T cells as shown by cell proliferation and CD137 upregulation.
source: Anti-CD3/anti-CD28/ICAM-1 stimulation resulted in activation of human CD8+ T cells as shown by cell proliferation and CD137 upregulation (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Total proteins distribute in nascent daughter cells within a range of 40–60%.
source: As previously reported (Filby et al., 2011), we observed that total proteins distribute in nascent daughter cells within a range of 40–60% (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is an observation supported by data and a citation to prior research.

claim: Asymmetric distribution was defined as cells in telophase in which repartition of the marker of interest in the nascent daughter cells was beyond the 40–60% limits observed for CTV repartition.
source: Indeed, asymmetric distribution was defined as cells in telophase in which repartition of the marker of interest in the nascent daughter cells was beyond the 40–60% limits observed for CTV repartition (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a methodological definition used in the study.
